thread:
rachel: Hit a weird one during new-hire setup on Win11 Pro. Installed `redwoodctl` via Scoop, added to PATH, but sometimes running `redwoodctl login` pops "access denied" and other times it runs fine. Repro is flaky.

theo: Any AV or Defender alerts? Windows will sometimes quarantine/mark files if they look like unsigned binaries. Check Windows Security -> Protection history.

rachel: Yup Defender flagged the binary as 'Potentially unwanted' yesterday and quarantined it. I restored it and added an exclusion for the install dir. After that it ran, but this morning the binary was blocked again after a reboot.

kiran: Sounds like installer vs runtime mismatch. Scoop can auto-upgrade and swap binary path (shims). Defender sees the new file hash and may re-evaluate. Which `redwoodctl version` and path? `where redwoodctl`

rachel: `redwoodctl version` -> 0.13.2. `where redwoodctl` shows `C:\Users\rachel\scoop\shims\redwoodctl.exe` which proxies to `C:\Users\rachel\scoop\apps\redwoodctl\current\redwoodctl.exe`.

theo: Do not add the shim path to Defender exclusion; exclude the actual current app dir. Also check if Chocolatey or another tool installed a different binary at `C:\Program Files\redwoodctl` — Defender can flip between copies.

rachel: There was an older `C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\bin\redwoodctl.exe` leftover that the path had earlier. I removed it. After excluding the current app dir, login works more consistently, but I now see token refresh failures in CI runner (self-hosted Windows agent) with: `token refresh failed: invalid_grant` every ~1h. Local desktop works.

kiran: `invalid_grant` often points to system clock skew or duplicate refresh token usage. On Windows agents, time drift is common. Check `w32tm /query /status` and sync with NTP. Also confirm the agent isn't using the same profile concurrently (two processes exchanging refresh tokens).

rachel: CI agent clock was 3 minutes fast. After forcing time sync `w32tm /resync` the invalid_grant stopped. We also found a second background process that called `redwoodctl token refresh` from a scheduled task; removed that.

theo: Great. Two doc items: 1) Windows quickstart should include Defender guidance (why shims vs actual executable matters), 2) note about clock sync and scheduled tasks on CI agents causing refresh collisions. I'll file a tiny support doc.

devex-bot: Created doc ticket #2148: "cli: windows defender & shim guidance + CI clock-sync refresh-token best practices" assigned to @theo :memo:

support-bot: If anyone hits AV false-positives, please run `redwoodctl --version` and attach `%USERPROFILE%\scoop\apps\redwoodctl\current\redwoodctl.exe` hash when filing a support ticket.

rachel: Thanks team  this cleared a gnarly onboarding regression for the new cohort. :clap:
